name: cc-config-switcher
description: Switch between Claude Code config directories (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) from a status bar item.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: A profile pinned in an untrusted folder is ignored until you trust it.

commands.title: Use Profile in This Window Only

claudeConfigSwitcher.defaultProfile.markdownDescription: Label of the profile every window uses unless a project pin or window-only choice says otherwise. Empty keeps whatever `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` VS Code was started with.

claudeConfigSwitcher.profile.markdownDescription: Profile label pinned to this project. Set it in **Workspace** settings, or run **Claude Code: Pin Profile to This Project**. Ignored until the folder is trusted.

claudeConfigSwitcher.profiles.markdownDescription: Profiles to choose from. `configDir` is the value written to `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: an absolute path, or one starting with `~` (expanded for you). Leave `configDir` empty (`""`) for the built-in default (`~/.claude`).

label.description: Name shown in the picker and status bar.

configDir.description: Absolute or ~ path for CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or empty for the default.

claudeConfigSwitcher.autoDiscover.markdownDescription: Also list every `~/.claude-<name>` directory as a profile named `<name>`, in addition to `#claudeConfigSwitcher.profiles#`.

claudeConfigSwitcher.colors.markdownDescription: Status bar color per profile label, e.g. `{ "work": "#c62828" }`. While that profile is active the whole status bar is tinted via `#workbench.colorCustomizations#`. Use **Claude Code: Set Profile Color** to pick one.

claudeConfigSwitcher.syncTerminal.markdownDescription: Also give new integrated terminals in each window that window's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so running `claude` there uses the same profile as the Claude Code panel.
